blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Three months after they left Egypt, the people of Israel camped at the foot of Mount Sinai. Moses told them to get ready, because on the third day God would meet with them.

verses.text: And it came to pass on the third day in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud; so that all the people that was in the camp trembled.

verses.text: And Moses brought forth the people out of the camp to meet with God; and they stood at the nether part of the mount.

verses.text: And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire: and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mount quaked greatly.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Fire, smoke, and a mountain shaking under their feet. These people had seen God part the sea. Now they were about to hear his voice.

verses.text: And when the voice of the trumpet sounded long, and waxed louder and louder, Moses spake, and God answered him by a voice.

verses.text: And the LORD came down upon mount Sinai, on the top of the mount: and the LORD called Moses up to the top of the mount; and Moses went up.

verses.text: And God spake all these words, saying,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And God spake all these words, saying,

verses.text: I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Before a single rule, God told them who he was and what he had already done. He had brought them out of slavery. Everything that followed came after that rescue.

verses.text: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

verses.text: Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

verses.text: And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then God spoke about his name, and about a day of rest.

verses.text: Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain; for the LORD will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain; for the LORD will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

verses.text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Six days of work, and then a day to stop. Sons and daughters, servants, strangers, even the animals would rest, because God rested on the seventh day after he made the world.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then God turned to how people live with each other, beginning at home.

verses.text: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.

verses.text: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The last word goes past what people do, all the way to the heart, where wanting what belongs to someone else begins.

verses.text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: On a shaking mountain, God gave his people words to live by. He did not give them to earn their way out of Egypt. He had already brought them out. These were the words of the God who rescued them, showing them how to love him and how to live in peace with their neighbors.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Exodus 19:16-20 and 20:1-17, the commandments themselves as scripture blocks, never paraphrased in God's voice; the sabbath is the text's own word with no position on which day; the rescue comes before the law, as 20:2 says.

cultural.note: Plain and reverent; no moralising beyond the text.

qa.rewritten: Free draft retold each commandment in narration before quoting it; rewritten around the verses.
